taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Chamaesyce angusta is normalized to the current accepted Euphorbia name.
look_here_first: Start with the silhouette: E. angusta is an erect perennial from a thickened rootstock, not a low sandmat. Distal leaves become strikingly linear to elliptic-linear—more than 6× as long as wide—and stems/leaves are usually short-strigose. Confirm with the strigose capsule and white 4-angled seed with low transverse ridges or wrinkles.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local legacy Chamaesyce source; current Kew accepts Euphorbia angusta, native from western Texas to Coahuila.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum. In E. angusta, the combination of erect perennial habit, very narrow distal leaves, uniform strigose pubescence, and hairy fruit is unusually distinctive.
morphology_keys.growth_form: Perennial with moderately to strongly thickened rootstock; stems erect, about 12–43 cm.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite. Proximal blades ovate to ovate-elliptic; distal blades linear to elliptic-linear, about 7–41 × 2–5 mm and more than 6× as long as wide. Base asymmetric, cuneate to rounded; margins entire; apex acute; surfaces usually short-strigose.
morphology_keys.stipules: Distinct, linear-subulate or reduced to nodiform/papilliform structures, often reddish brown, about 0.1–0.7 mm, strigose.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Solitary at distal nodes. Involucre strigose; 4 narrow oblong green to yellow-green glands with relatively showy white flabellate appendages whose distal margins are shallowly and irregularly toothed.
morphology_keys.fruit: Capsule broadly ovoid, about 2–2.6 × 2.5–3 mm, strigose.
morphology_keys.seed: Seeds white, ovoid, 4-angled in cross section, about 1.7–2.2 × 1.1–1.2 mm, transversely low-ridged or wrinkled.
best_field_traits: distal leaves linear to elliptic-linear and more than 6× as long as wide
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Against E. fendleri, E. angusta is much taller and erect, with very narrow distal leaves and a hairy capsule; E. fendleri is a low clustered perennial with rounded entire glabrous leaves and glabrous capsule. Against the prostrate sandmats, the erect narrow-leaved silhouette is the quickest first split.

comparisons.key_distinctions: The easiest field package is erect + narrow distal leaves + uniform short strigose hairs. The hairy capsule then confirms it against low glabrous-fruited perennial E. fendleri.

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia villifera: usually erect/ascending, but smaller-leaved and not defined by linear distal leaves
